descricao_original: In the duodenum, seen here, the submucosa also contains a mucus-secreting gland, named Brunner’s gland. This submucosal gland secretes an alkaline mucus that protects the intestinal mucosa from acidic gastric chyme. These glands are unique to the duodenal segment of small intestine and are most numerous in its proximal regions. 40x
creditos_identificados: Image source: This image was taken of a slide in the University of Virginia collection.

marcadores.explicacao_original: The initial 2-3 centimeters of the duodenum is intraperitoneal, the remainder is retroperitoneal until it joins with the stomach. Both regions of the duodenum are visible in this section. The region to the left is retroperitoneal and thus only an adventitia is present. The intraperitoneal section is to the right and is covered by a serosa consisting of the adventitia along with the visceral peritoneum.
